speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Maybe you should put on your Juicy pants again.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Good morning, Your Honour. Dr. Sheldon Cooper appearing in pro se. That is to say, representing himself.

speaker: judge_j_kirby
text: I know what it means. I went to law school.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: And yet you wound up in traffic court. Anyway, if it would please the court, I'd like to begin with an opening statement.

speaker: judge_j_kirby
text: The court would advise you to make it quick, as the court had a dicey-looking breakfast burrito this morning and just took an Imodium.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Very well, a quick opening statement. Like a milking stool, my case rests on three legs. I will demonstrate that I was improperly instructed in driving by a woman whose lack of respect for society borders on the sociopathic. I will argue that the emergency met the legal doctrine of quod est necessarium est licitum, that which is necessary is legal. But first, I will raise a Sixth Amendment issue. I'm unable to confront my accuser, a non-human entity, to wit, a camera. So, to sum up, improper instruction, quod est necessarium est licitum, Sixth Amendment. My milk stool is complete.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I object. You're completely ignoring the law.

speaker: judge_j_kirby
text: No, I'm following the law. I'm ignoring you.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: Really? I would point out that I am at the top of my profession, while you preside over the kiddy table of yours.

speaker: judge_j_kirby
text: Dr. Cooper, before I find you in contempt and throw you in jail, I'm going to give you a chance to apologize for that last remark.

speaker: sheldon_cooper
text: I am a scientist. I never apologize for the truth.
